repositoryConnection.heading: Repository connection
repositoryConnection.description: GitPM commits in the selected checkout and publishes its active branch directly to origin.
repositoryConnection.managedExternally: This connection is controlled by environment variables and is read-only here.
repositoryConnection.originHelp: GitPM publishes the active branch here and pulls updates. Provide an HTTP(S) or SSH URL with no embedded username, password, or token. Examples: http://gitlab.local/group/project.git, https://gitlab.example/group/project.git, git@gitlab.example:group/project.git.
repositoryConnection.gitlabSectionHelp: Required for OAuth login, member role checks, and Merge Requests. Without it GitPM can still publish over SSH or an HTTP(S) token, but Merge Requests are unavailable.
repositoryConnection.gitlabUrlHelp: Your GitLab address without the project path. Used for login and the GitLab API, not for git operations.
repositoryConnection.gitlabProjectHelp: A group/project path. It must match the path in the origin URL. Used for membership checks and Merge Requests.
repositoryConnection.clientIdHelp: The public OAuth Application ID of the GitPM app in GitLab (not a secret). If one GitLab field is set, all three are required and the origin URL must point to the same project on the same instance.
repositoryConnection.credentialNote: Do not enter passwords or tokens here. After saving, click "Sign in to GitLab": GitPM opens the GitLab authorization page, receives a short-lived token, and keeps it only in server memory — never in config, logs, or the URL. After a server restart you must sign in again. Plain HTTP sends credentials and repository data without encryption; use it only on a trusted local network.
repositoryConnection.sshNote: For SSH, access is provided by an administrator-provisioned key (GITPM_SSH_KEY_PATH or an ssh-agent). GitPM never stores, reads, or logs the key and never writes it to config. Use a passwordless URL above.
repositoryConnection.httpsTokenNote: For HTTP(S) without GitLab, access is provided by an administrator token (the GITPM_REMOTE_TOKEN environment variable). The token lives only in process memory and is never entered in this form. Plain HTTP sends it without transport encryption.
repositoryConnection.mrNote: Merge Requests are supported only for GitLab. Publishing over SSH or an HTTP(S) token pushes the branch to origin, but MR through GitPM is unavailable.
repositoryConnection.buttonsDisabledHint: "Sign in to GitLab" and "Test connection" become available once the GitLab block is filled in or an origin is configured, respectively.
repositoryConnection.securityHint: Use an HTTP(S) or SSH URL with no embedded username or password. Credentials stay only in server memory and are never written to Git configuration. Use plain HTTP only on a trusted local network.
repositoryConnection.changeConfirm: Change the publication origin to {url}? Existing local commits and files will not be changed.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_URL_INVAL: The repository URL is invalid: use an HTTP(S) or SSH URL with no embedded username, password, or token.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_URL_IN: The GitLab instance URL is invalid: provide the HTTP or HTTPS instance origin only, without the project path.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_PROJEC: The GitLab project is invalid: provide a group/project path.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_CLIENT: The OAuth Application ID is invalid.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_CONFIG: When configuring GitLab, all three fields are required: instance URL, project, and OAuth Application ID.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_REMOTE_RE: Set the origin URL first, then the GitLab parameters.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_REMOTE_PR: The origin URL and the GitLab project must identify the same project on the same GitLab instance.
repositoryConnection.error.REPOSITORY_CO: Confirm the origin change by repeating the request with the same confirmation value.
The connection is controlled by environment variables and cannot be changed from this form.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_NOT_CO: GitLab is not configured. Sign in after filling in the GitLab integration block.
repositoryConnection.error.SESSION_INVAL: The session is missing or expired. Sign in to GitLab again.
repositoryConnection.credentialNoteIdent: GitLab OAuth is used only for your identity and requests read_user. Fetch, push, role checks, and Merge Requests use the administrator-provisioned Project Access Token, which is never sent to the browser or stored in your session. Your GitLab Public email is required to create a commit.
